label: Population-genetic processes
text: BI.O.A4.1 Population-genetic processes. Natural selection: heritable variation that affects reproductive success changes allele frequencies. Drift is stronger in small effective populations. Hardy–Weinberg principle: with no selection, mutation, migration or drift (very large population), and random mating at an autosomal locus with discrete generations, allele frequencies stay constant. Under the same conditions genotype frequencies reach p², 2pq, q² after one generation. Nonrandom mating alone changes genotype frequencies, not allele frequencies. Hardy–Weinberg is a null model, not a mechanism. The Price equation partitions change in a mean trait into selection and transmission terms; it is an identity given defined fitness and trait values. Hamilton's rule (rB > C) holds under its derivation's assumptions, typically weak selection and additive fitness effects; its generality is CONTESTED. An evolutionarily stable strategy is the MA solution concept applied to fitness payoffs (uses MA.B.C4). Fitness is reproductive success in a stated environment.
